answer: In PoA, identity verification binds each claimed agent to a Wesolowski VDF: continuous modular squarings form a sequential chain, since each result is required before the next operation. An attacker can copy identities, but cannot parallelize one chain across GPUs to remove its delay; every clone requires its own sequential computation and hardware budget. This physical time bottleneck makes Sybil replication expensive, while a succinct proof verifies the completed chain efficiently for willow, umber, and garden.
